question: Does each periodic input reprocess old audio, or perform feature extraction over an unnecessarily long padded waveform?

configuration_profile.probe: CPU-only AutoProcessor with independent two- and four-second float32 waveforms, 16 kHz, deterministic Gaussian samples from numpy.default_rng(20260925), standard audio placeholder; torch.stft and WhisperFeatureExtractor._torch_extract_fbank_features wrapped to observe shapes and zero tail. change: Audit only for audio preprocessing; no feature-extractor configuration, model cache or installed dependency changed.

source_confirmed: The current first-party gateway sends audio accumulated since the previous tick and clears audioBuf; delayed ticks can accumulate more than one nominal period.
The worker sends only the current chunk in each StreamingInput; retained KV does not require repeating historical audio feature extraction.
Qwen2_5OmniProcessor forces padding=max_length. WhisperFeatureExtractor defaults max_length to n_samples before both STFT and mel computation.
The pinned model preprocessor config sets a long fixed window; the vLLM model processor applies feature_attention_mask only after the feature computation.
The trace IS/IE interval covers all InputProcessor.process_inputs, not an isolated STFT timer or GPU encoder event.
result.interpretation: The excess work is CPU feature computation on a zero-padded waveform. GPU encoder inputs are masked back to valid feature frames. Shape ratios do not establish runtime speedups.

remaining_uncertainty: No runtime fix or concurrent serving performance comparison in this audit.
A short-padding fix must preserve valid features including STFT boundary behavior, accept actual chunk length, and avoid truncating audio collected across delayed ticks.
No assertion that every production chunk contains exactly two seconds: payload duration depends on buffering and actual tick timing.
